leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members put the optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) as their sole prize part. They share the view that it is a single well-defined invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) with experimental confirmation by independent laboratories at the 1e-18 level and concrete consequences (redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, constants and dark-sector searches), and that a two-name credit is clean. They do not share a view on the timing question (several would not wait for the redefinition of the second, but the point is still raised by all five as a reservation), on how much weight the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes carry, on whether Katori's concept and Ye's realization are equal contributions, or on whether Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto and other groups should alter the credit. Two of the five (Johansson, Olsson) moved to B046 after opening, Johansson from sixth place and Olsson from third. The citation wordings differ only in emphasis.

Two members prefer the topological-insulator entry (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp). They agree that the Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall effect are a concept-level result, confirmed across HgTe, InAs/GaSb and Bi2Se3, and mature enough after roughly two decades. They differ in emphasis: Mehlig weighs it as the more conceptually original than a record-setting instrument, while Danielsson moved to it from inflation (B032) partly because of its broad cross-member support and wants the citation worded around the prediction and first observation so that it does not claim the HgTe proposal. Both accept that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are outside the credited names. B038 is also the most frequent alternative for the other camps (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce), but alternatives are not counted as supporters here.

One member prefers twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as a falsifiable prediction followed by experimental discovery, with a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, not the pairing mechanism. Eriksson acknowledges that the field is younger and the credit not fully clean (Cao, Fatemi, earlier continuum-model authors). Olsson, who ranked B042 first in opening, now lists it only as an alternative, so the explicit preferred-configuration support is a single member.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members propose a single-part prize; no member proposes a split into two prize parts or a configuration with more than one ballot ID.
Every member judges B046, B038 and B042 to be real, reproduced results; the disagreement is about credit, timing and novelty rather than whether the results are valid.

B046 and B038 are the two entries named by most members, either as preferred configuration or as first alternative; B038 is an alternative or preference for seven of eight members and B046 for seven of eight.

Members who prefer B046 and those who prefer B038 both identify B038's credit chain as incomplete, because Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and the 3D topological-insulator work lie outside the credited names.

Circuit QED (B006) is regarded as distinct in kind from the 2025 prize but is not preferred by any member as the leading configuration, and Johansson, who ranked it first in opening, now declines to be its principal advocate.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a discovery or invention in its own right or an advance of technique within a precision-timekeeping line honoured in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (single-ion control). Supporters point to magic-wavelength trapping and Lamb-Dicke confinement of many atoms as not contained in either prize; Danielsson and Mehlig weigh a clean new organising concept above a record-setting instrument.

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter makes a time-reversal-invariant Z2 prize a continuation or a distinct classification. Mehlig, Danielsson and Lindroth argue it is distinct; Eriksson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce treat the overlap as a real concern.
Whether B038 should cover only the 2D quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe or also the 3D topological insulators, which would bring in names outside the credited set.
Whether B042 should be recognised before the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is understood, or whether a citation limited to flat bands and observed correlated states settles the matter.
attribution_disputes: B046: whether Katori (concept and first strontium lattice clock) and Ye (record accuracy and stability, many-body clock physics) are best described as co-inventors or as inventor and realizer, and whether Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Schmidt and the Paris, PTB and Boulder groups are decisive enough that two names would be unfair. Kroll and Johansson would not widen the prize beyond two names; Olsson and Pearce treat the question as live.

B038: whether Kane, Mele and Molenkamp can be defended without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed the HgTe realization (Olsson notes Zhang has died); Danielsson would word the citation around prediction and first observation.
B042: experimental credit is concentrated on one group while Cao, Fatemi and the earlier continuum-model work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) are outside the credited names.

B006: four credited names for three places; Johansson would exclude Blais rather than Girvin, Olsson's view differs, and the supplied record does not resolve it. Members agree only that the three-person limit forces an exclusion.
maturity_disputes: B046 timing: whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the second. Kroll, Olsson, Johansson and Pearce say the prize need not wait; Lindroth, Olsson and Kroll list it as a reservation.

B042 timing: roughly eight years since the 2018 experiments, with the pairing mechanism disputed and the phase diagram sample dependent. Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce see it as better in a few years; Eriksson and Olsson argue reproduction across moire material families gives enough stability.

B006 timing: whether a circuit-QED prize is too close to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson raise it; Johansson argues it is physically distinct but accepts patience may be warranted).
B038 is the best matured of the leading entries (Mehlig, Danielsson), though the topological-phases prize of 2016 is raised against it.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-goran: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works in circuit QED at Chalmers, with Chalmers colleagues and a frequent co-author in the field; he ranked B006 first in opening, would consider recusing himself on B006 if it leads, and sees no tie to B046, B038 or the others.

Kroll-stefan: documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Jun Ye's group is at JILA in Boulder; no collaboration or personal relationship with Ye or Katori is documented, but he suggests the committee decide on recusal regarding Ye.

Eriksson-olle: chaired the 2025 prize committee, which bears on how B006 is weighed against the 2025 prize; he also works in two-dimensional materials theory at Uppsala, a neighbouring area to B042, with no documented tie to its credited names.

Olsson-eva: general link to Japanese academic exchanges, with Katori at a Japanese institution, and a Chalmers institutional link to Johansson; she documents no personal connection to Katori and no candidate-specific tie.
Lindroth-eva: works in atomic physics adjacent to B046; she documents no direct connection to Katori or Ye and flags the field closeness only for the committee to judge.

Pearce-mark (chair): no conflict for B046; PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO and XL-Calibur connections matter only for B025 (IceCube), which he is not proposing, and he would consider recusal from any decision on B025.
Danielsson-ulf and Mehlig-bernhard: no candidate-specific conflict disclosed for B038, B046 or B042.
questions_for_round2: B046: do the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems leave enough room for a lattice-clock prize, specifically on the magic-wavelength and many-atom Lamb-Dicke contribution that those prizes did not cover?
B046: should the committee wait for the redefinition of the second, or is the 1e-18 clock-to-clock agreement across independent laboratories sufficient evidence of maturity?

B046: is a two-name credit for Katori and Ye defensible given the contributions of Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Schmidt and the Paris, PTB and Boulder groups, and should the citation separate concept from realization?

B038: can a prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp be justified with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang outside the credited names, and would a citation limited to prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and first observation in HgTe quantum wells avoid the gap?
B038: does the 2016 topological-phases prize make a time-reversal-invariant Z2 prize a distinct achievement, and should it cover 2D only or also 3D topological insulators?

B042: can the unsettled superconducting mechanism be set aside by a citation limited to flat bands and observed correlated insulating and superconducting states, and how should Cao, Fatemi and earlier continuum-model authors be handled within three names?
Should Kroll's Boulder proximity (Ye at JILA) and Johansson's Chalmers circuit-QED role lead to any recusal or weighting adjustment, and does either affect the count of explicit supporters for B046?
summary.chair_observation: Explicit round-1 preferences are concentrated: five members prefer B046, two prefer B038 and one prefers B042, with no member preferring B006, B009, B017, B025, B032 or B033 as the lead. The B046 camp is the largest but each of its members records the same open reservations on prior prizes, timing and breadth of credit, while the B038 camp's central unresolved point is attribution. Where positions differ most is in how much weight to place on novelty relative to earlier prizes versus a clean attribution chain, and on whether timing should be tied to external decisions such as the redefinition of the second. Eight members were counted; no hidden votes are inferred.
